findings.title: Deleting the cache doesn't refresh connectedCalendars, so the old "Last updated" stays on screen
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike `disconnectMutation` (lines 61-64), it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-376` the wrapper gets no `onChanged`, and its query sets `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` (`SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:152-160`). After a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the old cache timestamp and the "Delete cached data" item, so the user is told a cache exists when it was just removed. Fix: add an `onSettled` that awaits `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`, the same as the disconnect mutation.

findings.title: `updateMany` with empty `data` probably never bumps `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`
findings.body: The comment says this updates `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. But `data` is `{}`, and as far as I know Prisma's engine only adds `@updatedAt` fields when the update has other fields, so an empty update writes nothing. The column is `DateTime? @updatedAt` (`schema.prisma:860`). Even if it did write, it costs an extra DB query on every webhook-driven cache refresh, and no code in this PR reads the value: the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, and the new `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` selects in `user.ts:899-900` and `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-28` are unused. Either set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly or drop the call and those selects. Also, because this runs after the cache upsert, a failure here fails the webhook even though the cache was already refreshed.

findings.title: Timestamp is always formatted with a hardcoded "en-US" locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's language from `useLocale` and shows US-style dates in a translated string. It also uses the browser timezone rather than the profile timezone. Pass the locale from `useLocale()` (and the user's timezone if available).

findings.title: Plain `Error` reaches the client as a 500, and the handler skips the existing repository
findings.body: Throwing `new Error(...)` from a tRPC handler becomes INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. A missing or foreign credential should be `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })`. Also, the PR body says this was moved to the repository pattern, but the delete calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly even though `CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential` already exists (see the interface and mock).

findings.title: Cache deletion is offered even when `disableConnectionModification` is set
findings.body: `hasCache` doesn't check `disableConnectionModification`, so the event-type Advanced tab (`EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375`, which passes `disableConnectionModification={true}`) now shows a destructive "Delete cached data" action. That action wipes the credential's cache for every event type, not just this one. Is that meant to be available from the event-type scope?

findings.title: `sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed, and `ENV_FILE` depends on the current directory
findings.body: On GNU sed (Linux), `-i ''` treats `''` as the script and the real expression as a filename, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the caller's CWD, not the script's location, so running it from the repo root writes to the repo's parent directory. Use something like `$(dirname "$0")/../.env`, and either a portable sed (`sed -i.bak … && rm`) or a temp-file rewrite. Also, `cleanup` exits 0 on the failure paths (lines 49, 57).

findings.title: Migration warning contradicts the SQL
findings.body: The header says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. Drop the stale Prisma-generated warning. Note too that every existing row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`, so "Last updated" will show the deploy time for legacy cache entries until they are refreshed.

contracts.action: Delete cached data via dropdown confirmation
contracts.equivalent_path: disconnectMutation in the same file, and MultiDisconnectIntegration, which invalidate connectedCalendars in onSettled
contracts.before_after: Disconnect invalidates connectedCalendars and integrations after the mutation; deleteCache only calls the optional onSuccess prop
contracts.visible_effect: Toast on success. The timestamp only refreshes if the parent's onChanged invalidates (CalendarListContainer does, EventAdvancedTab passes none)
contracts.failure_mode: onError shows an error toast. On success without onChanged, the stale cacheUpdatedAt stays displayed because refetchOnWindowFocus is false

contracts.action: Server deletes all CalendarCache rows for a credential
contracts.before_after: Ownership is checked right before the delete via findFirst on id+userId; the delete is scoped to that credentialId only
contracts.visible_effect: Rows are removed; availability falls back to live fetches until the next cache refill
contracts.failure_mode: A missing credential throws a plain Error (500). A deleteMany failure propagates to the client's onError toast. No journal involved

contracts.equivalent_path: SelectedCalendarRepository.updateById callers that pass real fields
contracts.before_after: Runs after the cache upserts with empty data
contracts.visible_effect: No UI consumer of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt in this PR
contracts.failure_mode: If it throws, the webhook handler fails after the cache was already written. With empty data, Prisma likely writes nothing
contracts.open_question: Does Prisma's query engine set @updatedAt on an updateMany whose data is {}?

contracts.before_after: groupBy max(updatedAt) per credentialId, ignoring expiresAt
contracts.visible_effect: Dropdown shows Cache Status for Google credentials with any cache row, even expired ones
contracts.failure_mode: A groupBy error fails the whole connectedCalendars query

summary: The main defect is in the new dropdown: deleting the cache never invalidates connectedCalendars. On the event-type Advanced tab, which passes no onChanged, the old \"Last updated\" timestamp and the delete action stay on screen after a successful delete. The Google webhook path calls updateMany with empty data, which probably doesn't bump updatedAt, and nothing reads that value anyway. Smaller items: a hardcoded en-US date format, a plain Error thrown in the tRPC handler, a direct Prisma call where a repository method already exists, cache deletion offered under disableConnectionModification, a dev script that only works with macOS sed, and a stale warning in the migration header.
